requirements.title: The landing conditions and the sync before a landing
requirements.rationale: A change that passed its review may still have to wait: for the person who paused it, for a main branch that is broken, or for an origin that moved.

criteria.action: for any item in the state `landing`, evaluate the landing conditions in this order and stop at the first that does not hold: neither the item nor its workspace is paused (`paused`); every condition registered with `AddCondition`, in registration order (its name); the workspace's state is `green`, or `red` for an item marked with `SetRepair` (`workspace red` or `workspace held`); the workspace's policy requires the three checks (`workspace held`); the sync from origin passes (`origin sync`); and report no check and send no land request while one does not hold
criteria.contract: `Service.Conditions(ctx, item)` returns the name of the first condition that does not hold, or the empty `Condition` when all hold; it is the evaluation the step runs, so it may hold the workspace for its policy and run the sync; for `paused`, a registered condition, `workspace red` and a workspace already `held` it returns without a request to the hub; an item that is not `landing` returns an error

requirements.title: A workspace held by its policy
requirements.rationale: Everything lands without the person only because the hub refuses a version nightshift has not checked; a policy that stopped requiring the checks removes that ground, and only the person can say whether it was meant.

criteria.condition: the conditions of an item in `landing` reach the policy, the workspace has no open `policy` decision, and `policy.Missing` of the policy read with the worker token names at least one requirement
criteria.action: set the workspace's state to `held` with `SetState`, append to the workspace's thread an entry of kind `workspace_state` with the text `green -> held: policy does not require nightshift's checks in: <names joined by ", ">`, open in that thread a decision of kind `policy` with the question `The policy of <slug> does not require nightshift's checks in: <names>. Adopt them?`, one piece of evidence per name, the options `adopt` (recommended) and `recheck` and `every landing in <slug>` as what it blocks, and call `Notify` of `internal/notify` with the event `workspace_held`, the workspace and the thread's URL path
criteria.contract: the workspace is `held`; `GET /api/v1/decisions` lists one `policy` decision with exactly the option keys `adopt` and `recheck`, neither requiring a comment, on the workspace's thread and with no item; the notifier received one `workspace_held` event; the item stays `landing` with no check reported and no land requested

requirements.title: The release check, the land request and the hub's answers
requirements.rationale: The hub lands what its policy lets pass, so nightshift's own conditions have to be a check on the hub, reported on exactly the version that is landed.

criteria.condition: every landing condition holds for an item in `landing` whose change the hub reports as `open` with `nightshift-gate` and `nightshift-review` `passed` on its current version
criteria.action: report the check `nightshift-release` as `passed` with the summary `conditions hold`, through `ReportCheck` of package 06, which reports on the change's current version, then ask the hub to land exactly the version it read with `LandChange` (`POST …/changes/{number}/land?wait=30` with the worker token and the body `{"expected_version": <version>}`, plus `session_id` when the change's `session_id` is not null), and append to the item's thread an entry of kind `land` with the text `land of version <version>: <the hub's answer>`
criteria.contract: `ReportCheck` was called once with `nightshift-release` and `passed` before the land request was sent; the land request names the version the step read as `expected_version`; `Service.Landing(ctx, item)` returns a `Record` with `ReleaseVersion` and `Release: "passed"`
